label: Postgres: Watch query
description: Keep a query's result live: run it now and on a cadence, and send it on the `rows` bus (every row) and the `row` bus (the first row) each time it differs from last time (pipe one into a Stream behind a Route for a live page). Parameters are inline-declared input ports read by name (`$userId`), as in Postgres: Query, and the build checks them the same way; one statement only. A `vector` or `halfvec` column comes back as a list of numbers; a column of a type the node cannot read refuses the query, so cast it (`weights::text`). With `channel` set it also LISTENs, so a `NOTIFY` from the database re-runs the query at once. A result with no rows sends `[]` on `rows` and `null` on `row`, and both stay open, since the next run may answer some. Runs until the run ends, then the buses close. The buses open with the first result: a query that fails before it is a failure `_error` can catch, and a failure after it ends the buses failed.

inputs.name: account
inputs.description: Wire a PostgresAccess, or a PostgresDatabase's access output.

inputs.name: query
inputs.label: SQL
inputs.placeholder: SELECT id, caption FROM cards ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 50
inputs.description: The one statement to keep live; each `$name` reads the input port of that name.

inputs.name: intervalSecs
inputs.label: Every (seconds)
inputs.description: Seconds between re-runs (at least 5): the whole cadence, or the backstop when `channel` is set.

inputs.name: channel
inputs.label: Notify channel
inputs.description: NOTIFY channel to LISTEN on; each notification re-runs the query. Empty polls only. Raise it from a database trigger whose function calls `pg_notify('cards_changed', '')`.

outputs.name: rows
outputs.description: One message per change carrying every row, `[]` when the query answers none (the first right after start).

outputs.name: row
outputs.description: One message each time the first row changes, carrying that row, or `null` while the query answers none (the first right after start).
